lines.text: Three settings that stop apps tracking you.
One: set location to While Using, so apps can't follow you when closed.
Two: turn off Precise Location, so apps see your area, not your door.
Three: switch off ad tracking, so apps lose the ID that follows you.
Two minutes, three switches. Save this, and do it tonight.

post.title: 3 settings that stop apps tracking you
post.caption:
3 settings that stop apps tracking you 📍

1. Location: While Using. Apps that say Always can read your location even when they are closed.
2. Precise Location: off. Weather and shopping apps only need your area, not your front door.
3. Ad tracking: off. On iPhone, apps then can't read the advertising ID that links you across apps; on Android, deleting the ID gives apps only zeros.

Two minutes, three switches. Save this for tonight, and send it to the friend who taps Allow on everything.

sources.note: Apple Support, Location Services: While Using the App allows access only when the app or its features are visible on screen; turn Precise Location off to share only your approximate location
Apple Support, If an app asks to track your activity: with Allow Apps to Request to Track off, apps can't access the advertising identifier (IDFA); Settings > Privacy & Security > Tracking
Android Developers: users choose Precise or Approximate, and While using the app / Only this time / Deny
Android Developers: approximate location is accurate to within about 3 square kilometers; precise usually within about 50 meters
Google Play Console Help, Advertising ID: when a user deletes the advertising ID (Settings > Privacy > Ads, Android 12+), apps reading it get a string of zeros
